task.title: Match paths against glob patterns
task.statement:
Write a JavaScript function `globMatch(pattern, path)` that tells whether a path matches a glob pattern. The whole path must match, and matching is case-sensitive.

Rules:
- `?` matches exactly one character other than `/`.
- `*` matches any sequence of characters other than `/`, including none. Several `*` in a row act as one, unless they form `**` as described next.
- `**` that makes up a whole path segment (it is at the start or right after `/`, and at the end or right before `/`) matches across segments:
  - `**` alone matches any path, including the empty one.
  - A leading `**/` matches zero or more whole segments, each followed by `/` (so `**/b` matches `b` and `x/y/b`).
  - A middle `/**/` matches `/` or `/` + any text + `/` (so `a/**/b` matches `a/b`, `a/x/b` and `a/x/y/b`).
  - A trailing `/**` matches `/` followed by anything (so `a/**` matches `a/` and `a/x/y`, but not `a`).
  - A `**` that is not a whole segment (as in `a**b`) acts like `*`.
- `[...]` matches one character other than `/` from a set: single characters and ranges like `a-z` (by character code). A leading `!` negates the set. A `]` right after `[` or `[!` is a literal member. A `-` first or last in the set is literal. `\` inside a set escapes the next character.
- `\` outside a set makes the next character literal.
- Every other character matches itself.
- Return `true` or `false`.
- Return `null` if either argument is not a string, or the pattern is invalid: a trailing `\`, an unterminated `[`, or a range whose start comes after its end.
